translationRepairs: Gao Huan accepted neither counsel, and thus came the defeat at Shawei.
Gao Huan accepted neither counsel, and thus came the defeat at Shaoyuan.
s0045 has 沙苑之敗; 沙苑 is Shaoyuan, not Shawei. The proposed romanization corrects a real place-name error while leaving the rest of the sentence intact.
The Grand Ancestor accepted neither counsel, and thus came the defeat at Shawei.
The Grand Ancestor accepted neither counsel, and thus came the defeat at Shaoyuan.
The literal line likewise mistranslates 沙苑 as Shawei; Shaoyuan matches the Chinese battle place-name.

Beguiled by her slander, he drove off his former wife, the Yu clan, and would not acknowledge his son. Resentment filled the household; one after another they reported him to the authorities. He was deeply scorned by the age.

Beguiled by her slander, he drove off his former wife of the Yu clan, and would not acknowledge his son. Resentment filled the household; one after another they reported him to the authorities. He was deeply scorned by the age.

前妻于氏 names the former wife as a woman of the Yu clan (née Yu). The appositive 'the Yu clan' wrongly equates her with the clan; 'of the Yu clan' restores the correct referent and aligns with the idiomatic.
Late in Xiaochang bandits rose everywhere. Seeing that the realm would soon fall into disorder, he went to Luoyang and befriended Murong Yan in the trade of hiring out horses.
Late in Xiaochang bandits rose everywhere. Seeing that the realm would soon fall into disorder, he went to Luoyang and befriended Murong Yan as a fellow horseman.
與慕容儼騎馬為友 means they became friends through riding horses together. The original invents a horse-hiring trade absent from the Chinese; 'fellow horseman' correctly removes that invention.
